onboarding.title: EVY × AERIS / agent start packet
onboarding.thesis: Deliver an approved capability centrally; verify, activate and execute it locally; preserve control and recover explicitly when connectivity or the executor fails.
onboarding.transfer: Signed deterministic joint-goal recipes. No remote code installation or trained-weight deployment is claimed.
onboarding.authority: Rust owns simulator execution. EVY dispatches immutable action requests. The browser observes and requests bounded lab operations. No physical motion is authorized.
onboarding.agent_prompt: Read AGENTS.md, docs/AGENT_START.md, onboarding/manifest.json, README.md and docs/PRESTON.md. Perform a read-only review of the architecture and source boundaries. Run python3 scripts/doctor.py --out evidence/readiness-001.json; exit 2 means missing prerequisites, not a hardware test failure. Explain what transfers, what runs locally, what the historical evidence proves, and what remains unproved. Ask only for missing target hardware, OS, topology, robot/controller and OEM-interface facts. Treat operator intake as unverified requirements, never measured evidence or executable commands. Within the user's authorized test scope, install project dependencies using scripts/setup.sh, rerun the doctor into a new evidence path, run scripts/check.sh, then prepare a NEW simulator session and use the documented browser challenge. Capture and independently audit its evidence. For two hosts, use the measured edge inventory and docs/PRESTON.md; role captures still need independent cross-host reconciliation. Report TDD/EDD/CDD/BDD/CBT with scoped red/amber/green, exact commands and source identities, retained failures and next blockers. Never reuse historical green as this host's qualification. Never read or share credential files in a report; never substitute robot or cluster passwords into the UI; never activate physical motion, disable TLS, change a kernel/driver, or change controller limits to make a test pass. Request the specific missing authorization only when the proposed operation exceeds this simulator test scope.
